source: Sudarshana's summary of the classics: the indications of each bhava (BPHS 11.2-13), their names (Phaladeepika 1.10-16), kinds (BPHS 32.35-37, Phaladeepika 1.17-18), karakas (BPHS 32.31-34, Phaladeepika 15.17) and limbs (Kalapurusha, BPHS 4.4, counted from the Lagna)

bhavas.name: Tanu
bhavas.about: The first bhava is the rising sign itself, the point where the native meets the world. It is the body and its make-up, the self, its vitality and its temperament, and it colours every other bhava, for each is counted from it. Parashara reads physique, appearance, intellect, complexion, vigour, weakness, happiness, grief and innate nature here. Both a kendra and a trikona, it is the most important bhava: a strong Lagna and Lagna lord carry the whole chart.

body: Marks and moles on the body

reading.strong: A strong first bhava and lord give a sound body, a long life, confidence and a good name, and the power to carry out what one begins; the native stands on their own feet and the rest of the chart works through them.
reading.weak: Afflicted, with its lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th or joined by malefics, it weakens health and vitality and brings illness, low confidence and struggle against circumstances. A benefic in a kendra or trikona is Parashara's remedy for the body (BPHS 12.1-2).

bhavas.name: Dhana
bhavas.about: The second bhava is what one holds: accumulated wealth, the family one belongs to, the food one eats and the speech one speaks. Parashara gives wealth, grains, family, death, enemies, metals and precious stones; Phaladeepika adds learning, the face, the right eye and written documents. A panaphara, and as the 7th from the 8th one of the two maraka bhavas, it also weighs on the span of life.

people: Family elders who keep its traditions

reading.strong: Wealth that grows and stays, a supportive family, sweet and truthful speech, good food and a pleasing face; learning comes easily and words carry weight.
reading.weak: Money that slips away or never gathers, quarrels in the family, harsh or untruthful speech and trouble to the eyes, teeth or face; as a maraka its dasa can bring illness late in life.

bhavas.name: Sahaja
bhavas.about: The third bhava is courage and effort: what one dares, the brothers and sisters one grows up with and the short journeys one makes. Parashara gives valour, servants, brothers and sisters, initiation into instruction (upadesh), journeys and the death of the parents; Phaladeepika adds the chest, the right ear and the army. An upachaya, it grows with time and with malefics in it, which give drive; as the 8th from the 8th it also bears on longevity.

reading.strong: Courage, enterprise and a fighting spirit; helpful brothers and sisters, success through one's own effort, and skill with the hands and with words.
reading.weak: Timidity or rash daring, strife with or loss of co-borns, trouble to the ears, arms or chest, and efforts that come to nothing.

bhavas.name: Bandhu
bhavas.about: The fourth bhava is the root of a life: mother, home, land and inner contentment. Parashara gives conveyances, relatives, mother, happiness, treasure, lands and buildings; Phaladeepika adds friends, cattle, perfumes, clothes, ornaments, water and rivers. At the nadir of the chart it is what lies beneath and behind: one's foundations, schooling and the peace of the heart.

reading.strong: A loving mother, a happy home, land, houses and vehicles, good schooling and a contented heart; the native is at ease wherever they live.
reading.weak: Unrest at home, distance from or worry for the mother, trouble over land, houses and vehicles, and an anxious, unsettled heart.

bhavas.name: Putra
bhavas.about: The fifth bhava is what one creates and what one has earned: children, intelligence, learning and the merit (purva punya) carried from past lives. Parashara gives amulets, sacred spells, learning, knowledge, sons, royalty and the fall from position; Phaladeepika adds the power of discernment (dhi), ministers, the belly, the Sruti and Smriti, and knowledge of what is to come. A trikona and the bhava of judgement, it shows how wisely one chooses and how one's creations prosper.

reading.strong: Good children, a sharp and discerning mind, success in learning, favour from those in power and the fruit of past merit; one's creations flourish.
reading.weak: Delay, worry or sorrow over children, poor judgement, interrupted studies, loss of position and losses in speculation.

bhavas.name: Ari
bhavas.about: The sixth bhava is struggle: enemies, disease, debt and the effort it takes to overcome them. Parashara gives the maternal uncle, doubts about death, enemies, ulcers and the stepmother; Phaladeepika adds debts, thieves, wounds, battles, fear and humiliation. It is a dusthana, yet also an upachaya: malefics here defeat enemies and disease, and it is the bhava of service and daily work.

wealth: Money lost to disputes and illness

reading.strong: Victory over enemies and rivals, good health and quick recovery from illness, freedom from debt, and success in service, competition and litigation.
reading.weak: Chronic illness, debts, troublesome enemies and lawsuits, theft, and trouble through servants or the maternal uncle.

bhavas.name: Yuvati
bhavas.about: The seventh bhava faces the first: the spouse and every partner one meets as an equal. Parashara gives the wife, travel, trade, loss of sight and death; Phaladeepika adds desire and passion, the roads one travels and the public. At the setting point it is a kendra and a maraka: it brings union and partnership, and with them the risks that come through others.

reading.strong: A good spouse and a lasting marriage, fruitful partnerships, success in trade and in dealings with the public, and pleasant travels.
reading.weak: Delay or discord in marriage, trouble to or from the spouse, failed partnerships and losses in trade; as a maraka, danger to health in its dasa.

bhavas.name: Randhra
bhavas.about: The eighth bhava is the hidden and the sudden: longevity, death and whatever comes unearned. Parashara gives longevity, battles, enemies, forts, the wealth of the dead and the things of past and future births; Phaladeepika adds obstacles, defeat, mental pain, blame and the auspiciousness of a marriage (mangalya). A dusthana, it is also where research, the occult and inheritance are found, for what is hidden can also be uncovered.

reading.strong: A long life, gains through inheritance and the unexpected, insight into hidden things, and the long life of the marriage (mangalya).
reading.weak: A short life or chronic illness, accidents, obstacles and sudden losses, disgrace and mental suffering.

bhavas.name: Dharma
bhavas.about: The ninth bhava is fortune and dharma: the grace one is born with, the teachers one follows and the faith one lives by. Parashara gives fortune, the wife's brother, religion, the brother's wife and visits to holy places; Phaladeepika adds the preceptor, the father, deities, worship, penance, merit and grandchildren. The strongest trikona, a good ninth lifts the whole chart.

reading.strong: Good fortune, a long-lived and helpful father, wise teachers, faith, pilgrimages and righteous deeds; luck comes when it is most needed.
reading.weak: Ill luck, strain with the father or teachers, loss of faith and acts against dharma.

bhavas.name: Karma
bhavas.about: The tenth bhava is what one does in the world: profession, position, honour and command. Parashara gives royalty, place, profession, honour, the father, living in foreign lands and debts; Phaladeepika adds commerce, fame, good conduct, sacrifices and the power to command. It is the strongest kendra, at the top of the sky, and a graha here is seen by all.

reading.strong: A respected profession, high position, authority and lasting fame; good deeds and success in what one undertakes.
reading.weak: Unsteady work and setbacks in career, loss of position or reputation, and strain with superiors or the father.

bhavas.name: Labha
bhavas.about: The eleventh bhava is gain: income, the fulfilment of wishes and all that flows in. Parashara gives all articles, the son's wife, income, prosperity and quadrupeds; Phaladeepika adds elder brothers and sisters, the left ear and pleasing news. The best of the upachayas, almost every graha does some good here, even a malefic.

reading.strong: Steady income, profits and gains from many sources, wishes fulfilled, and helpful elder brothers, sisters and friends.
reading.weak: Gains that do not come or do not last, unfulfilled hopes, and strained ties with elder siblings and friends.

bhavas.name: Vyaya
bhavas.about: The twelfth bhava is letting go: expenses, losses, sleep, distant lands and, at the end, liberation. Parashara gives expenses, the history of enemies and one's own death; Phaladeepika adds the feet, the left eye, the bed, poverty, sin and imprisonment. A dusthana and the last bhava, it shows where wealth and energy go, and a benefic here spends them well.

reading.strong: Money spent on good causes, restful sleep, comfort abroad and progress toward liberation.
reading.weak: Heavy and wasteful expenses, losses, sleeplessness, confinement or exile, and trouble to the feet or eyes.
